title: Skill learning and consolidation in healthy humans
description: This dataset comprises MEG, MRI, EMG, and eye-tracking data from 31 healthy right-handed adults performing a sequential finger tapping task (SFTT) to study early motor skill learning, overnight consolidation, and longer-term retention. Participants completed an initial MEG training session followed by up to two retest sessions approximately 24 hours and 30 days later, with resting-state MEG collected before and after each practice block. The dataset supports investigation of neural correlates of motor skill acquisition and memory consolidation.
methods_description: T1-weighted anatomical MRI volumes (1mm3 MPRAGE) were acquired on 3T scanners. Continuous MEG and EMG were recorded on a CTF-275 system at 600Hz sampling rate, with head position tracked via digitized coils. Behavioral responses were collected via E-Prime 2 and a Cedrus response pad, while eye gaze and pupillometry were recorded with an EyeLink 1000 Plus system synchronized to MEG. Participants practiced a 5-item finger sequence with their non-dominant hand across multiple sessions spanning an initial training day, a 24-hour retest, and a 30-day retest, interspersed with resting-state scans.
